name: Wangfujing Snack Street
description: Beijing's most famous snack street. Touristy but convenient, with everything from scorpion skewers to candied fruit.

name: Jinli Ancient Street
description: A restored ancient street with lanterns, traditional architecture, and dozens of authentic Sichuan snack stalls.

name: Muslim Quarter
description: Xi'an's vibrant Muslim Quarter is a sensory overload of sizzling grills, aromatic spices, and halal street food.

name: Yunnan Road Food Street
description: Shanghai's historic food street lined with century-old snack shops. The go-to for authentic xiaolongbao and shengjianbao.

name: Jiefangbei / Bayi Road
description: Chongqing's central food hub serving the city's famously intense spicy snacks in a bustling night market atmosphere.

name: Shangxiajiu Pedestrian Street
description: Guangzhou's classic shopping and eating street, lined with century-old bakeries like Lian Xiang Lou and street-side cheong fun stalls.
